title: MV Talk to party members on the field? (Party chat feature)

posts.author: Dusk_Funa
posts.body:
I've found it for other versions of RPG Maker, but I was wondering if there was any MV-specific plugin somewhere that allowed the player to interact with their party members while on the field. Something like: Walk up next to/above party member > press action button > a dialogue occurs (preferably where a bust image appears).
The dialogue presented would change depending on the map, current player progression, and preferably would also allow for a pool of generic banter in case the player has not yet reached any new dialogue flags; while also including banter that only occurs once (say, right after the player obtains a key item for a side quest).
I've seen plugins like YEP's Gab Window, but it's not the vision I have for my project.
The gif below of another MV game is an accurate example of what I'm looking for, but its plugins are proprietary/unreleased so I would rather not touch them. I could do without the choice window appearing and just have dialogue there.
If there somehow is a way to do this with events-- which seems like a very daunting task, I would also be willing to learn how to do so.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
In your example picture, the player is NOT talking to a party member, but to an independent event pretending to be a party member.
you can see the difference due to the movement as party members only follow the party leader without any form of independent movement. Which is the main problem with that idea, because the player can't move to a follower to trigger it.
there are only two possibilities how this can be done without rewriting the entire follower system:
either you watch for a keypress and trigger the conversations beginning with a selection which actor to talk to and never walk up to a follower to select it.
or you transfer the party to a map where the followers are hidden and replaced with events pretending to be them, which of course means this won't happen on the usual game maps (this is often implemented in a camp-map).

Click to expand...
I don't know dark souls, but most likely yes - it has been used in many games.
Basically you'll have an item "tent" or so that transfers the player to a different map (or several different based on original map ID), with followers disabled and replaced by events on that camp map.
Just have one event per possible actor, conditioned to actor in party, and only those who are in the party will appear there.
and then you can go around, talk or heal or craft or whatever you want until sleep, which will bring the player back to the original map.

Took a bit of trial and error to get the hidden choices going, but after some deliberation I believe the meeting spot option is best!
I wanted to use Hime's plugin but couldn't figure out how to make it so a choice doesn't appear if a specific follower isn't present (forgive my complete ignorance for code), but Aloe's worked out! Tyruswoo's Follower Control seems useful but I do plan on setting up an ABS plugin in the future. A little afraid of using that before the ABS is in place and everything just breaks. The "gather followers" command does the job for now.
But now comes the part of dialogue. I believe it'd be far more convenient to use a common event (no matter how large it turns out to be), so I have centralized control of everything each party member says at these meeting spots but... I simply have no idea how to implement that aside from the "run common event" command after selecting to talk to an available party member lol.
To rephrase my original post, dialogue should not only include generic banter for if the player hasn't reached new progression flags or is just spamming the talk option, but new dialogue can be added to that pool with each checkpoint discovered or progression flag reached, while also including banter that only occurs once during, say, something like a side-quest right after the player obtains a key item for it. Maybe mjshi's talk to follower plugin that got recommended could be handy, or at the very least the basics of how it was set up...? I know it must sound like a big ask, but maybe you or someone else lurking has the answers.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
new message adding is best by simple plugin with events.
so you can push the message in and select 1 at random or
change the line to a new one.
the same can be achievement if you use 1 variable per actor
and change that line if required and call it with `\v[3]`.
there are some ways for that, so how the progression works and
how to check them is up to you.
pre-defined into a plugin to read the variable value (fixed for each actor),
you can set up the actor id switch with variable ID value (case 0, case 1, etc).
so you can automate the text that is defined and setup through the entire game.
you can try to wrap around it, see what fit, use map or npc events of actors,
or variable value to call with `\v[number]` and it shows for that actor.
or each their own to simplify things easier.
as for the ABS, that can harder, or easier, depending which one you gonna use.
